summary: The note describes "Art for All," an inclusive arts program launched by the New Horizons Art Center on September 5th, 2023 under Director Mariana Gomez. It covers workshops in schools, eldercare facilities and community centers, adaptive tools for artists with disabilities, a cultural mural project, youth sessions, and an October 15th exhibition. It closes with plans for a permanent community art studio and a grant for free year-round classes.
one_line: New Horizons Art Center's "Art for All" program brings workshops, adaptive tools, murals and exhibitions to underserved and diverse communities, with a permanent studio planned.
key_facts: The New Horizons Art Center launched the "Art for All" program on September 5th, 2023, spearheaded by Director Mariana Gomez.
Art for All aims to foster artistic engagement among people with disabilities, the economically disadvantaged, and people from various cultural and age groups.
On September 12th, art instructors held workshops at Jackson Middle School, where children are often denied art due to budget cuts.
On September 19th, a workshop at the Autumn Leaves Retirement Home had elderly residents painting from wheelchairs, aiming to combat loneliness and stimulate mental health.
Art therapist David Zhou developed adaptive tools and techniques for aspiring artists with physical disabilities.
Zhou's September 26th workshop at the City Community Center used modified brushes that could be held in the mouth or attached to wheelchairs.
A mural project began on October 2nd in the Easton District, led by local artists Sofia Martinez and Jamal Adebowale, depicting the district's history and diversity.
On October 9th at Lakeside Park, teens from different socioeconomic backgrounds made digital and traditional art under multimedia artist Alex Chen.
A showcase on October 15th at the New Horizons Art Center displayed work from the outreach program, from landscapes by the elderly to portraits of inner-city life by high schoolers.
Fourteen-year-old Maya Rodriguez displayed digital illustrations on October 21st depicting her battle with social anxiety.
On November 1st, plans were announced for a permanent community art studio.
A grant has been secured to provide free art classes year-round.
